title: Revisiting Reliability in Large-Scale Machine Learning Research Clusters
problem: Large-scale ML training clusters suffer from frequent job failures whose impact on training efficiency is not well characterized across different job sizes and cluster configurations. Existing failure models do not adequately capture workload diversity or provide actionable metrics like Effective Training Time Ratio (ETTR).
motivation: As ML models scale to thousands of GPUs, even rare hardware or software faults cause disproportionate disruption, yet no rigorous taxonomy or quantitative framework exists to guide infrastructure and algorithmic reliability investments.
method: The authors conducted an 11-month observational study across two large multi-tenant A100 GPU clusters totaling 4 million jobs and over 150 million GPU-hours. They developed a failure taxonomy, computed Mean Time to Failure (MTTF) as a function of GPU count by fitting a failure model to operational data, and derived an analytical estimator for Effective Training Time Ratio (ETTR) as a function of job parameters (checkpoint interval, restart overhead, failure rate). The ETTR model is used to project the efficacy of software mitigations such as more frequent checkpointing.
key_novelty: Introducing the Effective Training Time Ratio (ETTR) metric and its analytical model, enabling quantitative projection of software mitigation strategies across different GPU scales.
contributions: An 11-month empirical dataset covering 4 million jobs and 150 million+ A100 GPU-hours with a structured failure taxonomy.
A fitted failure model that projects MTTF as a function of GPU job scale.
An analytical ETTR estimator parameterized by job size, checkpoint interval, and restart overhead.
Operational insights showing smaller jobs dominate job count and must be included in reliability optimization objectives.

metrics.other: MTTF projected for various GPU scales; ETTR derived analytically; 4M jobs, 150M+ A100 GPU-hours analyzed

baselines: prior infrastructure reliability studies (no single named system baseline)
limitations: The study is limited to two specific Meta/industry clusters and may not generalize to other hardware vendors or open-source cluster configurations.
primary_theme: ML cluster reliability and failure characterization
